chaldeans.title: Chaldeans
chaldeans.note: They started as one tribal group in southern Mesopotamia and ended up ruling the whole Babylonian empire. In the Old Testament the name came to mean Babylonians in general.

cushan.title: Cushan
cushan.note: In Habakkuk's poem the tents of Cushan tremble alongside Midian as the Lord approaches. Probably a Cushite group in northwest Arabia, not African Cush, and no relation to the king Cushan-rishathaim. Where exactly it lay is not established.

god.title: God
god.note: The Bible never argues that he exists; it assumes it, and Psalm 14:1 calls the man who denies it a fool. The Hebrew is El, from a word meaning strong, or Eloah, far more often in the plural Elohim. Jehovah, the other name, is printed LORD in small capitals in the Authorized Version.

habakkuk.title: Habakkuk
habakkuk.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
habakkuk.note: He argued with God. Why does Judah's injustice go unpunished, he asks, and when the answer is Babylon, he asks how God can use a nation worse than Judah to do it. The book ends with him choosing to trust and rejoice with his questions still open, and his line that the righteous will live by faith is one Paul built on.

lebanon.title: Lebanon
lebanon.note: Two mountain ridges along the coast, Lebanon proper to the west and the Anti-Lebanon rising to Mount Hermon, with the Beqaa Valley between. Solomon's temple and palace were built of its cedar, cut and floated south under a deal with Hiram of Tyre. Israel was promised it and never took all of it.

midian.title: Midian
midian.note: A people descended from Abraham through Keturah, and they keep turning up in different roles. Midianite traders bought Joseph. Moses found a home and a wife, Zipporah, in Midian. Later they oppressed Israel until Gideon beat them.

paran.title: Paran
paran.note: Ishmael grew up in this wilderness after Hagar was sent away with him, and Israel camped there for part of the long march.
